newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma wheat condition declines slightly.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma wheat condition declines slightly.

text.p: Oklahoma wheat condition declined slightly during January due to dry conditions and light freeze damage, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday.
Moisture was needed in most areas to continue proper development of the wheat, the service said in its crop weather report, which is released monthly during winter months.

Oklahoma wheat condition was rated five percent excellent, 69 good, 23 fair and three fair. That compared to three percent excellent, 75 good, 21 fair and one percent poor at the beginning of January.
Livestock conditions remained mostly unchanged, the report said. The recent upward trend in cattle prices has increased marketings in many areas.
Topsoil moisture was rated adequate to short and subsoil moisture was rated mostly adequate.
